finalText:
I've worked the dock and monitor backorders: 14 lines are allocated, 4 lines that are still waiting have promise dates, and 14 customers have been notified. Two more supplier deliveries were marked received while I worked: PO-91 (4 docks) and PO-93 (3 monitors). The task only named PO-88 and PO-89, but the handbook says all received stock goes to backorders in priority order, so I allocated these too. Without them the waiting lines would have been promised later dates while the units sat on the shelf.

**How I ranked orders.** The store system's date is 2026-07-25, not the 2026-10-06 in my own context, and I used the store's date. That matters: if 2026-10-06 were "today", every order would count as aged and priority would follow order date alone. One policy update (PU-12) applies from 1 July: orders placed 14 or more days ago (on or before 2026-07-11) go first, oldest first. Everyone else follows by tier (platinum, gold, standard), then earliest order. The other update (PU-9, gold ranked with platinum) only covered June, so I didn't apply it.

**Allocated (stock set aside, ready for the warehouse to ship):**
- **Docks (11 units, now 0 left):** O-5201 (2), O-5202 L2 (1), O-5204 (2), O-5207 L1 (1), O-5210 (1), O-5209 (2), O-5211 (1), O-5215 (1)
- **Monitors (7 units, now 0 left):** O-5202 L1 (1), O-5203 (2), O-5207 L2 (1), O-5208 (2), O-5212 (1)
- O-5207 has to ship as one parcel, and both its lines could be filled together, so both were allocated.

**Still waiting, with promise dates:**
- **O-5206:** this order also has to ship as one parcel, and its USB-C hub line has no stock, so its dock line waited too. The dock comes from PO-95 (2026-08-14) and the hub from PO-90 (2026-08-06). Both lines are promised for the later date, 2026-08-14.
- **O-5213:** needs 2 docks; only 1 was left when its turn came, so it waits for PO-95, promised 2026-08-14. The last dock went to O-5215, next in line.
- **O-5214:** monitor from PO-97, promised 2026-08-19.

**Left alone:** O-5205 (1 dock) is on risk hold, so it got no stock, no promise date and no message.

**Customers:** each of the 14 other orders got one message, sent after its lines were allocated or promised. Orders ready to ship were told so; the three waiting orders were given their expected ship date.
